JUDGMENT BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE:
1. On 11.11.2022, vide GD No.50A information was received at PS Govind Puri regarding suicide on which IO / SI Vivek Tomar alongwith Ct.
Rakesh went to the spot i.e. B-444, Transit Camp, Govind Puri where caller / accused Arjun Dass met and told that his wife has hanged herself and the door of the room was closed from inside.
IO got the door opened after cutting its lower part with gas cutter and found one lady Gita hanging by a ceiling fan.
IO called the crime team and crime team inspected the spot and took photographs.

Body of deceased was sent to AIIMS hospital and informed SDM, Kalkaji about the death who recorded statement of father of deceased on 12.11.2022.
2.
In his statement Sh. Pawan Kumar Das, father of deceased stated that his daughter got married to Arjun Das on 26.01.2017.
His daughter studied upto 8th class and was working as domestic help.
His son-in-law was working as delivery boy in a General Store and after he lost his job, he started misbehaving and beating his daughter.
He used to take all the money earned by Gita and spent it on other woman and liquor.
His son-in-law was having affair with some other woman because of which he used to beat and torture his daughter.
This fact was told by Gita whenever she came to her parental home.
His daughter used to come every 15-20 days to seek money from him.

4 plan, arrested the accused vide arrest memo already Ex.PW-6/A, recorded disclosure statement of accused, seized the mobile phone make REDMI of accused vide seizure memo already Ex.PW-6/D and deposed about the investigation conducted by him.

20. Accused admitted the copy of MLC report No. 9493/2022 dated 11.11.2022 as Ex.X1, copy of FIR Ex.X2, copy of DD No.50A dated 11.11.2022 as Ex.X3, scale site plan as Ex.X4, Crime Scene Report as Ex.X5 and FSL report as Ex.X6 u/s. 294 Cr.PC.
21.

Thereafter, prosecution evidence was closed vide order dated 30.05.2024 and matter was fixed for recording statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
22.

The statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 06.06.2024 in which he denied the allegations and submitted that he has been falsely implicated in the present case and he did not want to lead any defence evidence.
Thereafter, final arguments were heard.

23. I have heard the arguments advanced by the Ld. Addl. PP for the State and Ld. LAC for the accused and have perused the record......
24.

In order to prove the offense U/s 306 IPC against accused, the prosecution was required to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused tortured his wife Gita and was having extra marital affair because of which Gita committed suicide.
Henceforth, court shall now proceed further to evaluate the evidence available on record to find out if the prosecution has succeeded in its task or not.
25. Section 306 of The Indian Penal Code, 1860 defines Abetment of suicide and same is reproduced here in below:-

306 . Abetment of suicide :- If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
The most important ingredient for the offence u/s. 306 IPC is that suicide should have been committed by the deceased.
Deceased Gita was found hanging by ceiling fan in room which was locked from inside and same was got opened after getting it cut through gas cutter.
As per prosecution case in the room only dead body of deceased Gita was found and no other person was inside the room.
Therefore, the only conclusion that can be drawn was that the deceased herself bolted the door from inside.
Further, PM report Ex.PW-8/A shows the cause of death as "asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging".
This proves that death of the deceased have occurred due to the hanging.
So, it is proved beyond doubt that deceased committed suicide by hanging herself with chunni after bolting the room from inside.
26. Next important ingredient for culpability U/s. 306 IPC is that accused should have abetted the Suicide.
Gita got married with accused Arjun on 26.01.2017 and Gita committed suicide on 11.11.2022.
Therefore, Gita committed suicide within 7 years of her marriage.

When a married State vs Arjun Das on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75160222/
5 woman commits suicide within 7 years of her marriage, a presumption is drawn regarding the abetment of her suicide U/s 113A of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and the relevant provision is reproduced here in below:-
Sec113A. Presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman.

sentences.text: - When the question is whether the commission of suicide by a woman had been abetted by her husband or any relative of her husband and it is shown that she had committed suicide within a period of seven years from the date of her marriage and that her husband or such relative of her husband had subjected her to cruelty, the court may presume, having regard to all the other circumstances of the case, that such suicide had been abetted by her husband or by such relative of her husband.
Explanation - For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" shall have the same meaning as in section 498A of the Indian Pena l Code (45 of 1860).]

27. It has been held in "Mangat Ram v. State of Haryana", AIR 2014 SC 1782, that the mere fact that if a married woman commits suicide within a period of seven years of her marriage, the presumption under section 113A of the Evidence Act would not automatically apply.

entities.text: Mangat Ram v. State of Haryana", AIR 2014 SC 1782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Legislative mandate is that where a woman commits suicide within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that her husband or any relative of her husband has subjected her to cruelty as defined under section 498A IPC only then the presumption under section 113A of Indian Penal Code, may attract,
having regard to all other circumstances of the case, that such suicide has been abetted by her husband or by such relative of her husband.
The term "the court may presume, having regard to all other circumstances of the case, that such suicide had been abetted by her husband" would indicate that the presumption is discretionary.

28. So, The presumption under Section 113A of the Indian Evidence Act will only be fastened if it is proved that accused has committed cruelty upon the deceased as defined under section 498A IPC,
which is reproduced hereinbelow :-
Section 498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

In "Hans Raj Sharma Vs Govt of NCT of Delhi", Crl.A.No.339- 41/2005 decided on 2 March,
2010, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held at para10, which is reproduced herein below:-
"10.

entities.text: Hans Raj Sharma Vs Govt of NCT of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to succeed in charge under Section 498-A IPC, the prosecution was required to prove that the appellants had subjected deceased Lovely to cruelty, as defined in the explanation to the Section.
It is not every cruelty which is punishable under Section 498-A of IPC.
The cruelty, as defined in the explanation to 498-A of IPC, is altogether different from the cruelty, which can be subject matter of proceedings, under the provisions of Hindu Marriage Act.

The cruelty, so as to attract penal provisions, contained in Section 498-A of IPC, has necessarily to be a willful conduct which is of such a nature that it is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or cause grievous injury or danger to her life or health.

The use of the expression "willful" in the explanation to Section 498-A of IPC indicates that the conduct attributed to the accused, in order to be culpable, needs to be deliberate, aimed at causing injury to the health of the woman or bringing misery to her.

If the accused knows or is reasonable expected to know that his conduct is likely to cause injury to the life, limb or health of the aggrieved woman or if his conduct is of such a nature,
that causing injury to the life, limb or health can be a natural consequence for the woman, who is recipient of such a conduct, it will attract criminal liability on the part of the husband or his relative, as the case may be.
Everyone is presumed to intend the natural consequences of his act and such a presumption must necessarily be drawn even if there is no intention to cause any injury or harm to the woman.

Whether the conduct in question is likely to drive the woman to cause injury to her life, limb or health, will depend upon a number of factors such as social and economic status of the parties, the level of awareness of the aggrieved woman, her temperament, state of her health, physical as well as mental and how she is likely to perceive such a behavior.

If a woman is harassed with a view to coerce her or any of her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security, it will also constitute cruelty, as defined in the explanation to Section 498-A of IPC.

Of course,
the expression "cruelty" would take in its ambit mental cruelty as well as physical torture of the woman.

If the conduct of the accused with a woman is likely to cause a reasonable apprehension in her mind that her living with the husband will be harmful and injurious to her life and safety, such a conduct would attract criminal liability, envisaged in Section 498-A of IPC."
30. Sec.498A IPC has two explanations (a) and (b). The explanation (b) talks about the harassment related to unlawful demand of any property or valuable security but same is not the case of the prosecution as no allegations regarding any demand of property or valuable security has been made against the accused or his family members by the family of the deceased.

PW-1 Pawan Kumar, PW-2 Jitender Dass and PW-3 Smt. Shanta, who were father, brother and mother of deceased respectively did not deposed anything about demand of any dowry article by the accused, PW-1 only deposed that he gave washing machine to accused out of love and affection and specifically deposed that his daughter never came to his house for demanding anything.
Therefore, explanation (b) is not applicable in the present case.

sentences.text: Explanation (a) of Sec.498A IPC says that if the conduct of the accused is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or cause danger to her mental health then it will amount to cruelty.
The allegations against the accused made by the family of the deceased are that he was having an extra marital affair.

No doubt extra marital affair of the husband will definitely cause grave mental cruelty to the married woman and can also drive her to commit suicide, so, if accused had extra marital affair which his deceased wife came to know about then definitely his conduct i.e. having extra marital affair, will amounts to cruelty under explanation (a) of Sec.498A IPC but for that it is necessary that prosecution has proved that accused had extra marital affair.
32.
Prosecution has relied upon PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3, who are the father, brother and mother respectively of deceased, to show that accused has extra marital affair.
PW-1 has specifically deposed that he has never seen accused with any other woman.
PW-2 deposed that he mentioned that accused had illicit affair in his statement out of anger and PW-3 also deposed that out of anger she has given false statement to the police.
This shows that PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 all turned hostile and did not depose anything about extramarital affair of accused.
33. Further, during investigation IO examined the call record of the accused but he could not find any mobile number on which accused was talking regularly.
Family of the deceased did not provide anything regarding extra-marital affair of accused during the investigation.

Considering that no evidence regarding extra-marital affair of the accused has been brought on record by the prosecution, therefore, prosecution failed to prove that accused have any extra-marital affair.
34. Another allegation made against the accused was that he used to torture the deceased.
PW-1 stated that accused only once torture his daughter but later on with his intervention the dispute got settled.

PW-2 specifically stated that in his statement he stated that accused used to beat his sister out of anger and PW-3, who is the mother of the deceased and must be the person to whom deceased must have confided everything, has specifically stated that deceased has never told her that accused either misbehaved with her or harassed her or assaulted her.

So, no allegations of any torture are made by PW-2 and PW-3 and only a vague allegation regarding torture has been made by PW-1 with no details like date or month or the nature or the kind of torture given by the accused to the deceased.

Regarding the alleged incident of beating given to the deceased Gita on 10.11.2022 i.e. day before her death, PW-2 specifically stated that Gita suffered injuries as she fall down on a bench in the kitchen.
Therefore, prosecution failed to prove any kind of torture given by the accused to the deceased.

35. No other type of cruelty or any other incident of cruelty have been alleged by the prosecution against the accused, therefore, no cruelty as defined under Sec.498A IPC was subjected upon the deceased by the accused.
Therefore, no presumption under Sec. 113A of the Indian Evidence Act can be fastened upon the accused.
36. Prosecution has failed to prove that accused has abetted the suicide committed by deceased Gita.
Accordingly, accused Arjun Das is acquitted of the charge under section 306 IPC.

Accordingly, accused Arjun Das is acquitted of the charge under section 306 IPC.
